h1:
Samut Prakan in 2 Days, 1 Night
Ancient City, Pak Nam, Bang Pu
intro: Samut Prakan sits right next to Bangkok — you can get there on the BTS Green Line — so a lot of people write it off as a morning-out, back-by-evening kind of trip. But honestly, if you stay one night you get to take it slow: the sprawling Ancient City easily eats a whole day, Pak Nam still has its old cross-river ferry that carries you over to Phra Samut Chedi, and Bang Pu draws flocks of migrating seagulls every cool season. This is a relaxed, easy-walking 2-day 1-night plan with times, entry fees and prices we've actually checked.

blocks.html: This plan starts where most people do — arriving mid-morning. Day one goes all-in on Ancient City because the place is huge; half a day won't cover it. Late afternoon you stop by the Erawan Museum on the way to your hotel. Day two heads into Pak Nam town, where you take the cross-river ferry over to pay respects at Phra Samut Chedi, wander the old market, then close out the trip at Bang Pu in the late afternoon — timed for the birds and the sunset. The pace is kept light, with room to sit down for some seafood by the water.

blocks.title: How to get around
blocks.html: From Bangkok you can ride the BTS Green Line straight here. Chang Erawan station drops you right at the Erawan Museum, the end of the line at Kheha station is near Bang Pu, and Pak Nam station puts you at the old town and the ferry pier. But if you're doing Ancient City and Bang Pu, the easiest option is to drive yourself — both are large and sit off the BTS line. In town you can fill gaps with motorbike taxis and songthaew pickups.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: A full day at Ancient City + Erawan Museum

items.activity: Arrive at Ancient City in Bang Pu — start early to dodge the midday sun
items.note: Ancient City is open 09:00–19:00 daily. Entry for Thai adults is 400 THB, children 200 THB, seniors 60 and over free, and foreigners 800 THB. The grounds are so vast that a full day still won't cover everything — you can rent a bicycle on site or hop on the tram that loops around.

items.activity: Walk the cluster of replica monuments from all over Thailand
items.note: Inside are scaled-down replicas of temples, palaces and prasats from every region, laid out geographically like a map of Thailand. Highlights include the Sanphet Prasat throne hall, a replica of Khao Phra Wihan, and wooden waterside pavilions. Wear comfortable shoes — there's a lot of walking.

items.activity: Lunch break inside Ancient City — the old floating market
items.note: Ancient City has a replica floating market with Thai food stalls and old-style desserts where you can sit and rest. Prices aren't too steep — it's a good spot to put your feet up before carrying on through the afternoon.

items.activity: Continue through the Northern–Isan zones, photograph the wooden bridges
items.note: By afternoon the sun softens and the zones you haven't covered are easier walking. If you're tired, take the tram loop to pick up the spots you missed. If you're only coming for the afternoon, buying your ticket between 15:00–18:00 gets you the half-price rate of 200 THB.

items.activity: Leave Ancient City, stop by the Erawan Museum
items.note: The Erawan is the giant green three-headed elephant statue you can spot from far away. It's open 09:00–18:00 with the ticket counter closing at 17:00; entry is 250 THB for Thais and 400 THB for foreigners. BTS Chang Erawan station puts you right there. Inside it's decorated with stained glass and detailed stucco work.
Hotels in central Samut Prakan and the Bang Na–Theparak area come in a range of price levels. For dinner, try a made-to-order spot or seafood in town. Save your energy for the next day.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Pak Nam, the Phra Samut Chedi ferry + Bang Pu in the evening

items.activity: Head into Pak Nam town, walk Pak Nam Market
items.note: Pak Nam Market is around Si Samut Road, an old wet market that locals have used for generations. You'll find breakfast options — congee, dim sum, noodles — plus dried seafood. You can walk over from BTS Pak Nam, on the way to the ferry pier.

items.activity: Take the cross-river ferry from Wibun Si pier to Phra Samut Chedi
items.note: The ferry costs 6 THB per person, crossing the Chao Phraya River to the Phra Samut Chedi side. It's the boat locals genuinely ride every day; the last crossing is around 21:30. Once across, it's about a 600 m walk to the chedi.

items.activity: Pay respects at Phra Samut Chedi, the old mid-river chedi
items.note: Phra Samut Chedi was built back in the reign of Rama III and restored under Rama IV. It was originally an island in the middle of the river, so Pak Nam locals still call it the 'mid-river chedi.' Entry is free, and the riverside setting is quiet and peaceful.

items.activity: Ferry back to the Pak Nam side, seafood lunch
items.note: Pak Nam sits at the mouth of the river, so the seafood is very fresh. Try a seafood place in town or by the water — order stretched prawns, blanched cockles, steamed blue crab, bold Pak Nam-style flavors. Prices go by the weight of that day's catch.

items.activity: Go to Bang Pu, walk Suk Ta pier to watch the birds
items.note: Bang Pu Recreation Center is open 05:30–20:00 with a low entry fee per car/person. The highlight is Suk Ta pier reaching out over the sea, with shops and bird-feeding spots. In the cool season (Nov–Apr) tens of thousands of seagulls migrate in from Siberia — you can buy crackers to feed them.

items.activity: Watch the sunset at Bang Pu, wrap up the trip
items.note: In the evening a cool sea breeze rolls in — it's the prettiest time of day at Bang Pu. Sit down for seafood by the water at one of the spots inside the recreation center, or a well-known place in the Bang Pu area, and catch the sunset before heading home.

items: 1 night's stay — hotels in town start around 500–900 THB; mid-range places on the main roads run 1,000–1,800 THB
Ancient City — Thai adults 400 THB, children 200 THB, seniors free (afternoon 15:00–18:00 drops to 200 THB)
Phra Samut Chedi ferry — 6 THB per person, 12 THB round trip, free entry to the chedi
Bang Pu — entry is a few tens of baht; budget another few hundred to a couple thousand for waterside seafood depending on what you order
Food for 2 days — street food and seafood around 500–900 THB

blocks.title: When's the best time to go
blocks.html: If you want to see the full flocks of seagulls at Bang Pu, you need to come in the cool season, November–April, when the birds migrate in. Outside that window you can still stroll the seafront at Bang Pu, just without the birds. Ancient City involves a lot of open-air walking, so avoid the harsh midday sun — starting early or going in the late afternoon is more comfortable. In the rainy season pack an umbrella, since both spots are mostly outdoors.

blocks.text: Can you do it as a single day trip?

blocks.html: You can, but you'll have to pick one focus, because Ancient City alone eats up nearly the whole day. If you're only going for a day, we'd suggest splitting it two ways. Option one: go all-in on Ancient City, then swing by the Erawan Museum in the evening. Option two: skip Ancient City entirely, focus on Pak Nam and Phra Samut Chedi in the late morning, then head to Bang Pu to watch the birds in the evening. Staying one night lets you hit all three without rushing — well worth it if you have the time.

items.name: Ancient City
items.blurb: An open-air museum gathering scaled-down replicas of monuments from all over Thailand. It's huge and takes a full day — walk it, cycle it, or ride the tram.

items.name: Phra Samut Chedi
items.blurb: An old mid-river chedi dating to the reign of Rama III, reached by a 6-THB cross-river ferry from Pak Nam — a genuine slice of local life.

items.name: Bang Pu
items.blurb: A recreation center on the Gulf of Thailand with Suk Ta pier reaching over the sea. In the cool season come tens of thousands of seagulls and sunset views.

faq.q: Is 2 days and 1 night enough for Samut Prakan?
faq.a: It's just right. Day one goes all-in on Ancient City since the place is huge, then you stop by the Erawan Museum in the evening. Day two heads into Pak Nam town, takes the cross-river ferry to pay respects at Phra Samut Chedi, then closes the trip at Bang Pu watching the birds in the evening. You get culture, river and sea without rushing.

faq.q: How much is Ancient City and what are its hours?
faq.a: It's open daily 09:00–18:00. Entry is 400 THB for Thai adults, 200 THB for children, free for seniors 60 and over, and 800 THB for foreigners. If you come only between 15:00–18:00 there's a half-price ticket at 200 THB. The grounds are vast, so renting a bicycle or riding the in-park tram is recommended.

faq.q: How much is the cross-river ferry to Phra Samut Chedi?
faq.a: The ferry is 6 THB per person, leaving from Wibun Si pier near Pak Nam Market and crossing the Chao Phraya to the Phra Samut Chedi side. It's the boat locals genuinely ride every day, with the last crossing around 21:30. Once across, it's about a 600 m walk to the chedi.

faq.q: When can you see the seagulls at Bang Pu?
faq.a: Flocks of seagulls migrate in from Siberia to Bang Pu every year during the cool season, roughly November to April, arriving by the tens of thousands. The evening near sunset is the prettiest time. You can buy crackers to feed the birds at Suk Ta pier. Outside this season you can still stroll the seafront, just without the birds.

faq.q: Can you get to Samut Prakan by BTS?
faq.a: Yes — the BTS Green Line now extends to Samut Prakan. Chang Erawan station drops you at the Erawan Museum, Pak Nam station puts you at the old town and ferry pier, and the end of the line at Kheha station is near Bang Pu. But Ancient City and Bang Pu sit off the BTS line, so it's easiest if you drive yourself or take local transport in town.
